stem: Vestigial organ ____ present in human body is proof of evolution.
solution: The vermiform appendix is a vestigial organ in the human body. It is a functionless remnant of the caecum which was well developed and useful in herbivorous ancestors. Its presence is anatomical evidence of evolution. (Human hand is a functional homologous organ, while ear muscles and tail-bone are also vestigial but the classic textbook example asked here is the appendix.)

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Type of sexual reproduction is ____.
solution: Gamete formation (formation of male and female gametes followed by their fusion) is a feature of sexual reproduction. Fragmentation, regeneration and budding are all methods of asexual reproduction that do not involve gametes.

stem: The apex consumer is ____.
solution: In a food chain grasshopper (primary consumer) is eaten by frog, frog by snake, and snake by eagle. The eagle is at the top of the food chain and is not eaten by any other consumer, so the eagle is the apex (top) consumer.

stem: The Hydroelectric capacity of Koyna dam is ____.
solution: The Koyna hydroelectric project in Maharashtra has a total installed generating capacity of 1960 MW, making it one of the largest hydroelectric power plants in India.

stem: Animal with bilateral symmetry is ____.
solution: Human body can be divided into two equal (mirror-image) halves by only one median plane, so it shows bilateral symmetry. Adult star fish shows radial symmetry, Paramoecium is asymmetrical, and Amoeba has no definite symmetry.

stem: State whether the following statement is true or false: To take selfie on road is the invitation for accident.
solution: True. Taking a selfie on a road or at a dangerous place distracts attention and puts the person in the path of vehicles or in a risky spot, which can easily cause a serious or fatal accident. Hence it is an invitation for accident.

stem: Write the correct co-relation: Insulin : diabetes :: Interferon : ____.
solution: Interferon : viral infections (viral diseases). Just as insulin is used to treat diabetes, interferon is a protein produced by biotechnology that is used to treat viral infections (and certain cancers).

stem: To which class does bat belong?
solution: Bat belongs to Class Mammalia. Although it can fly, it has mammary glands, hair on the body and gives birth to young ones, so it is a mammal.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 1
stem: Give scientific reason: Sometimes higher plants and animals too perform anaerobic respiration.
solution: Normally higher plants and animals carry out aerobic respiration using oxygen. But when oxygen supply becomes insufficient, they perform anaerobic respiration to obtain energy without oxygen. For example, in the roots of waterlogged plants and in our muscle cells during vigorous exercise, oxygen falls short, so glucose is broken down anaerobically (in muscles it forms lactic acid). Thus, to keep meeting their energy demand under low-oxygen conditions, higher plants and animals sometimes perform anaerobic respiration.

stem: Give scientific reason: It is absolutely necessary to control the fission reaction in a nuclear power plant.
solution: In a nuclear power plant, energy is obtained from a controlled nuclear fission chain reaction. If the chain reaction is not controlled, the number of fissions increases rapidly, releasing an enormous amount of energy in a very short time (like a nuclear bomb), which can cause a dangerous explosion and radiation leakage. To produce energy safely and steadily, the reaction is controlled using control rods (which absorb excess neutrons) and a moderator. Hence it is absolutely necessary to control the fission reaction in a nuclear power plant.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Give scientific reason: Flower is the structural unit of sexual reproduction in a plant.
solution: A flower contains the essential reproductive organs of a plant: the stamens (androecium) which are the male reproductive organs producing pollen grains (male gametes), and the pistil/carpel (gynoecium) which is the female reproductive organ containing ovules (female gametes). Pollination and fertilisation take place in the flower, after which the ovary develops into fruit and ovules into seeds. Since both male and female gametes are produced and their fusion begins here, the flower is the structural (functional) unit of sexual reproduction in a plant.

stem: Write a short note on Environmental Conservation.
solution: Environmental conservation means the protection, preservation and wise (sustainable) use of natural resources and the environment so that ecological balance is maintained. It involves conserving forests (afforestation, preventing deforestation), protecting wildlife and biodiversity, controlling air, water and soil pollution, conserving water and soil, and using resources judiciously through the 3 R's — Reduce, Reuse and Recycle. Governments enact laws (such as the Forest Conservation Act, Wildlife Protection Act) and set up sanctuaries, national parks and biosphere reserves. Public awareness and individual participation are essential to conserve the environment for present and future generations.

stem: Distinguish between Chordates and Non-chordates.
solution:
Chordates vs Non-chordates:

| Chordates | Non-chordates |
|---|---|
| A notochord is present at some stage of life | Notochord is absent |
| Dorsal, hollow, single nerve cord is present | Nerve cord, if present, is ventral, solid and double |
| Pharyngeal gill slits are present at some stage | Gill slits are absent |
| Post-anal tail is usually present | Post-anal tail is absent |
| Heart is ventral | Heart, if present, is dorsal or lateral |
| Examples: fish, frog, lizard, birds, humans | Examples: Amoeba, sponges, earthworm, star fish, cockroach |

solution:

1. Regeneration and repair of damaged tissues and organs (e.g. skin, bone, cartilage).
2. Treatment of diseases and disorders such as leukaemia and other blood disorders through bone-marrow (stem cell) transplant.
3. Treatment of degenerative conditions like diabetes, Parkinson's disease, spinal cord injuries and burns; and growing tissues/organs for transplantation.

stem: Write down any two objectives of disaster management.
solution: Any two objectives of disaster management: (1) To minimise the loss of human life, property, livestock and natural resources during a disaster. (2) To provide prompt rescue, relief and medical aid to the affected people and to rehabilitate them. (Other objectives: to prevent or reduce (mitigate) the impact of disasters, to create public awareness and preparedness, and to ensure quick recovery and reconstruction.)

stem: What are the benefits of mixing ethanol with petrol and diesel?
solution: Benefits of blending ethanol with petrol and diesel: (1) Ethanol is a renewable fuel obtained from biomass (sugarcane molasses, etc.), so it reduces our dependence on limited fossil fuels and saves foreign exchange spent on importing crude oil. (2) Ethanol burns more completely and cleanly, so it reduces harmful emissions such as carbon monoxide and unburnt hydrocarbons, lowering air pollution. (3) It improves the octane number and efficiency of combustion of the fuel. Thus ethanol-blended fuel is more eco-friendly and economical.

stem: Explain Darwin's theory of natural selection.
solution:
Charles Darwin proposed the theory of natural selection in his book 'On the Origin of Species'. Its main points are:
1. Overproduction: Every species produces many more offspring than can survive.
2. Struggle for existence: Because natural resources (food, space, mate) are limited, there is a constant struggle for survival among individuals.
3. Variations: Individuals of a species show small variations; some variations are favourable and some are not.
4. Survival of the fittest: Individuals with favourable variations are better adapted to the environment, so they survive and reproduce, while the less-adapted ones are eliminated. Nature thus 'selects' the fittest — this is natural selection.
5. Inheritance of favourable variations: The favourable variations are passed on to the next generation. Over many generations these accumulate, gradually giving rise to new species. This process is called evolution by natural selection.

stem: Write the factors affecting the environment.
solution:
The factors affecting the environment are of two types:
1. Abiotic (non-living) factors: air, water, soil, temperature, sunlight (light), humidity, rainfall, pressure and minerals.
2. Biotic (living) factors: plants (producers), animals (consumers), and micro-organisms (decomposers), and their interrelationships.
In addition, human activities such as deforestation, urbanisation, industrialisation and pollution greatly affect the environment. All these factors together determine the ecological balance of an environment.

context: Refer to the figure of a hydroelectric power station showing the reservoir wall with three marked levels — A (top), B (middle) and C (bottom) — the sluice gate, penstock, turbine, generator and power house.
stem: With reference to point B, the potential energy of how much water in the reservoir of the dam will be converted into kinetic energy?
solution: The water flows out to the turbine through the intake/penstock at level B. Therefore only the water lying above the level of point B — i.e. the water column between point B and the free water surface at the top (level A) — has a head above the outlet, and it is the potential energy of this water (the water above point B) that gets converted into kinetic energy as it rushes down the penstock to the turbine.
figureNote: Cut-section diagram of a hydroelectric dam/power house with reservoir levels A, B, C marked on the wall, sluice gate, penstock, turbine, generator, power house and transmission towers, p-06.

context: Refer to the figure of a hydroelectric power station showing the reservoir wall with three marked levels — A (top), B (middle) and C (bottom) — the sluice gate, penstock, turbine, generator and power house.
stem: What will be the effect on electricity generation if the channel taking water to the turbine starts at point A?
solution: Point A is near the top of the reservoir. If the intake channel starts at A, the height (head) of the water column above the intake is very small and only a little water is available above that level. Hence the potential energy, and therefore the kinetic energy of water reaching the turbine, will be low. As a result the turbine rotates slowly and electricity generation will decrease (be much less).
figureNote: Same hydroelectric dam cut-section figure with levels A, B, C, p-06.

context: Refer to the figure of a hydroelectric power station showing the reservoir wall with three marked levels — A (top), B (middle) and C (bottom) — the sluice gate, penstock, turbine, generator and power house.
stem: What will be the effect on electricity generation if the channel taking water to the turbine starts at point C?
solution: Point C is at the bottom of the reservoir. If the intake channel starts at C, the entire column of water above C (the maximum head of water) is available, so the water has maximum potential energy which is converted into maximum kinetic energy at the turbine. The turbine rotates fast and the electricity generation will be maximum (highest).
figureNote: Same hydroelectric dam cut-section figure with levels A, B, C, p-06.

chapter: Life Processes in Living Organisms Part 2
stem: Cockroach, Frog, Sparrow, Star fish — from these animals, which one can regenerate its broken body part?
solution: Star fish can regenerate its broken body part. If an arm (and part of the central disc) of a star fish breaks off, it can grow back a complete new body, i.e. star fish shows regeneration. Cockroach, frog and sparrow do not regenerate lost body parts in this way.

stem: Complete the diagram showing the various processes (steps) in tissue culture.
solution:
The steps of plant tissue culture shown in the cyclic diagram are:
1. Explant: a small piece of plant tissue (e.g. from a bud/shoot tip) is taken from a healthy plant.
2. Culture in nutrient medium (sterile flask/bottle): the explant is placed in a sterile nutrient medium containing plant hormones.
3. Callus formation: the explant divides repeatedly to form an undifferentiated mass of cells called callus.
4. Shooting and rooting: the callus is transferred to another medium where it differentiates and develops shoots and roots, forming tiny plantlets.
5. Transplantation of plantlets: the plantlets are transferred to pots/soil, where they grow into complete new plants.
figureNote: Cyclic diagram of plant tissue culture with several blank boxes and images (mother plant, callus, culture bottle, box labelled 'Shooting and Rooting', plantlets), to be completed, p-07.

stem: Which fuels are obtained from biomass?
solution: Fuels obtained from biomass include: (1) Biogas (mainly methane, from gobar gas plants), (2) Bio-ethanol/ethanol (from fermentation of sugarcane molasses and other plant material), (3) Bio-diesel (from vegetable oils/plant seeds), and (4) solid biomass fuels such as firewood (wood) and charcoal. These are renewable fuels produced from plant and animal matter.

stem: In the menstrual cycle, which reproductive organs undergo changes?
solution: During the menstrual cycle two reproductive organs mainly undergo changes: (1) the ovary (development of follicle, ovulation, formation of corpus luteum and corpus albicans) and (2) the uterus, specifically its inner lining the endometrium (its thickening and shedding).
figureNote: Same menstrual cycle diagram showing changes in the ovary and the uterus (endometrium), p-09.

context: Refer to the diagram of the menstrual cycle showing the hypothalamus (GnRH), pituitary glands (FSH, LH), changes in the ovary during menstruation (developing follicle, fully grown follicle, ovulation, corpus luteum, corpus albicans), hormones estrogen and progesterone, and the changes in the uterus (endometrium) over days 1 to 28.
stem: Which period is said to be the period of regeneration of the endometrium?
solution: The proliferative phase (also called the follicular or regeneration phase), which extends from about day 5 to day 14 (after the menstrual flow and up to ovulation), is the period of regeneration of the endometrium. During this phase, under the influence of estrogen, the endometrium of the uterus is repaired and thickened again.
figureNote: Same menstrual cycle diagram; endometrium regenerating during days 5-14, p-09.

context: Refer to the diagram of the menstrual cycle showing the hypothalamus (GnRH), pituitary glands (FSH, LH), changes in the ovary during menstruation (developing follicle, fully grown follicle, ovulation, corpus luteum, corpus albicans), hormones estrogen and progesterone, and the changes in the uterus (endometrium) over days 1 to 28.
stem: Which period is said to be the period of secretions of the glands in the endometrium?
solution: The secretory phase (also called the luteal phase), which extends from about day 15 to day 28 (after ovulation), is the period of secretion of the glands in the endometrium. During this phase the corpus luteum secretes progesterone (and estrogen), under whose influence the endometrial glands become active and secrete nutritive fluids to prepare the uterus for possible implantation of the embryo.
